title: Fractional Fidelity Onramp — personal sketch
content:
Context / high-level idea:

We want a low-friction way to let new users (and low-intent trial flows) experience Redwood-powered assistants without paying full token/latency costs up-front. The onramp offers 'fractional fidelity' — short, cheap micro-responses or progressive previews that reveal more compute / model capacity as the user engages or converts.

Why this feels useful:
- Trials often die because first impressions are slow or expensive. If the first few turns are terse but fast, users can test flows quickly.
- Teams building assistants want a predictable pathway from demo -> paid usage. Fractional fidelity can be instrumented to nudge conversion.
- Platform-level feature (not product UI) — provide primitives (API flags, response tiers, SDK helpers) that apps can opt into.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Offering a 2–3 turn micro-response preview will increase trial activation (time to first meaningful reply) by ~50% and reduce perceived latency.
- H2: Showing an inline "upgrade to high fidelity" CTA after the preview will yield ~3–7% conversion to paid tier in a targeted cohort.
- H3: Overall token spend per user during discovery decreases while net conversion revenue increases (unit economics improve).

Rough product primitives (what the platform must expose):
1) fidelity_level param (enum): micro, compact, standard, full. Micro = < 32 tokens, small model variant, aggressive sampling to reduce latency.
2) preview_window: number of free micro turns allowed before prompting.
3) upgrader hook: optional callback/redirect from SDK for inline upsell / switch to standard fidelity.
4) metrics + labels: tag sessions with fidelity_level, converted_at, preview_used to compute lift.
5) graceful fallthrough: SDK should be able to auto-fallback to cached prefix or standard model if user upgrades mid-turn.

MVP proposal (minimal viable integration):
- API flag: fidelity_level="micro" + preview_window=3
- Client SDK: a helper that shows an upgrade chip once preview_window exhausted
- Dashboard: new funnel viz (preview started -> preview completed -> upgrade CTA shown -> upgrade accepted) + cost-per-conversion metric

User stories (for rough PRD):
- As a new app user, I want a fast first reply so I can judge the assistant quickly. Acceptance: first reply < 300ms P50 for targeted region on hosted models.
- As a developer integrating Redwood, I want a single flag to enable fractional fidelity so I can A/B test without migrations. Acceptance: single request header or SDK option toggles behavior.
- As a product manager, I want to see preview funnel metrics so we can decide to broaden rollout. Acceptance: dashboard shows cohort conversion and avg token spend.

Technical constraints / implementation notes:
- Need small model shards or quantized variants that are cheap to serve; coordinate with runtime team (ENG-2384).
- KV cache implications: micro responses should not write large KV for preview-only interactions (to avoid polluting session state). Offer ephemeral cache mode.
- Canary routing: preview traffic should prefer low-cost capacity (spot/dedicated micro-pool) but must be able to promote to standard capacity on upgrade.
- Billing: preview turns billed at fractional token rate or zero? For MVP bill at 10% listed token rate and mark as preview in usage logs for later reconciliation.

Metrics to measure (initial):
- time_to_first_reply P50/P90 for preview vs control
- preview_to_upgrade conversion rate (cohorted by channel)
- avg tokens consumed per trial user (first 7 days)
- revenue per trial user (30d)
- error/fallback rate when promoting from micro->standard

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- UX: do we show the response truncated with a "Show full answer (upgrade)" button, or send separate micro + full responses?
- Billing model: free vs fractional charge. Free increases load, fractional charge reduces abuse but complicates accounting.
- Model quality: micro answers may hallucinate more. Risk of harming perception. Need guardrails: for micro mode, favor conservative decoding / higher temperature control and label responses accordingly.
- Privacy/security: ensure preview cache doesn't persist sensitive content if ephemeral by design.

Experiment plan (first 6 weeks):
Week 0–1: infra spike with runtime + billing: simple fidelity flag atop existing endpoints (no UI).
Week 2: instrumenting telemetry + thin SDK helper. Launch internal QA + SRE smoke tests.
Week 3–4: small external beta with 3 partners (developer customers) using preview_window=2. Collect metrics.
Week 5: iterate UX: test inline upgrade vs modal.
Week 6: decision gate for broader rollout based on conversion delta and token spend.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Sync with serving-runtime (Rory/Sam) about micro-pool feasibility — create ENG ticket.
- [ ] Draft billing recommendation for finance/legal (fractional vs free).
- [ ] Prototype SDK helper component for web demo (Tess).
- [ ] Write initial dashboard spec for product analytics (Maya).

Quick notes / friction points to remember:
- Keep band-aids minimal: do not over-index on per-user personalization in preview — we want predictable, cheap compute.
- Watch for abuse: preview offering might be gamed for free tokens (rate-limit aggressively).
- Communication: front-end should mark preview content as "Preview (short answer)" to set expectations.

Random brainstorming seeds (ideas to explore later):
- Loyalty credits: give n free preview windows per billing cycle to engaged users.
- Micro-UI: animated "thinking dots" with "peek" that shows a 1-line digest while backend computes full answer.
- Pay-per-upgrade: user pays a small micro-fee to unlock full fidelity for this session only (transactional upsell).

Notes to self: rough, messy — prioritize telemetry early. Keep MVP surface tiny: flag + SDK helper + dashboard funnel.
